bounds: One continuation token with a stable platform redirect, one exact Telegram session, two phones, two lineages and two account pairs. Age 2 represents expiry. The token shard serializes decisions. Session inspection and claim publication are projected as a single decision over an authoritative observed session. Trusted external account redemption is modeled as one publication compatible with the admitted claim, including a completion in flight across expiry. Identity cryptography, redirect collision or mutation, cross-shard inspection races, storage write failures, account linking and transcript migration are separate.

assumptions: No scheduling fairness. An admitted request uses the observed trusted session and keeps the original lineage and pinned account.
No scheduling fairness. The account binding comes from authorized external redemption and completion reads that binding.
Weak fairness of exactCleanup. When a claim remains after a matching durable account bind, a caller eventually presents the exact completion and its deletion succeeds.
No scheduling fairness. A crash or missing completion call can retain a bound claim indefinitely.
